newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Consultant heats up Chicago soybean market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Consultant heats up Chicago soybean market.

text.p: US soybean prices posted double-digit gains and pulled wheat and corn (maize) up with them in Chicago commodity trading on Wednesday.
Influential US consultant Willard Sparks said he expected old crop soybean prices to rise, traders said.
Sparks told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday that Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) soybean prices are set to rise sharply because of tight U.S. soybean stocks.
The Agriculture Department earlier this month put soybean ending stocks at a tight 125 million bushels.
Sparks compared this year's soybean market potential to last year's corn market action which took prices to record highs.
In early trading, soybeans were up 17 to 5-3/4 cents per bushel with July up 16-1/4 at $8.82.

The soybean rally and weather forecasts sparked a rise in wheat futures. Lack of rain in the US growing regions which could delay planting and the end of a brief rainy spell in Europe were the principal price factors.

In Chicago May delivery wheat was 11-1/2 cents higher at $4.22-1/2 and on the London futures market, July last traded 0.30 stg higher at 96.00 stg and most active month January last traded 1.00 stg higher at 98.50 stg.
A late recovery lifted an otherwise quiet coffee futures market although London was slow to follow the move which began in New York and stretched the price differential between the two centres.
Dealers said the price firmed on rumours of supply problems in the major South American producers Colombia and Brazil
The Colombian harvest could total less than 10 million bags this crop year, traders said.
There was also buying coming into the market against the first cold snaps of the season in Brazil next month.
Cocoa futures prices were easier however as it became clear that speculators were unlikely to take delivery of large tonnages of cocoa when the current futures contract expires later this week.
The price responded with losses mainly on the nearby months. "But we expect the price to move lower across the board in the near term," one trader said.
Gold and silver prices were barely changed from Tuesday's close although latest US economic data were interpreted as showing signs of inflation which encouraged buying.
"US data coming through with some inflationary signals is about the only thing gold has going for it at the moment," a bullion dealer said.
Gold is traditionally a store of value for savings in times of high inflation but market confidence has been broken by threats that sales of gold from central bank vaults would crush prices.
The copper price charged higher in late trading to nearly $2,380 a tonne n tight supplies and a background of strikes, either actual or threatened, at two of Chile's major mines.
